For more information on Lion Street, please go to www.lionstreet.com.

objectives.

jobs.title: Director of Sales Technology - Remote
jobs.description:
Are you looking to accelerate your career without having to hide your authentic self - a place where you can be you? A career that’s making a bigger impact on the world? At OneDigital, we are on a mission to help people do their best work and live their best lives. From the services we offer to the way we show up for each other each day, we are fueling dreams, achieving big goals, and embracing each other’s truest selves.

We understand that pursuing a new job is a big deal. Maybe you’re afraid you won’t fit in. Well, here’s the good news. For us, the days of “fit in to get in” are over and being different is not a barrier to getting ahead. Greatness comes in all shapes, sizes, colors, and experience levels. If you are looking for a people-first culture that is wired for growth, driven to serve, and totally committed to having your back, give us a shot. Your best life awaits.

Must be eligible to work in the United States without the need for work visa or residency sponsorship.

We kindly ask that external recruiters, agencies, and search firms do not contact our hiring managers or employees directly regarding open positions. All candidate submissions must go through our official application process and must be made aware to our internal Talent Acquisition team to verify candidate ownership.

Unsolicited resumes or candidate profiles sent to OneDigital without a prior signed agreement will be considered the property of OneDigital. In such cases, OneDigital reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidates without any financial obligation to the agency or recruiter.

Our Newest Opportunity

As Director of Sales Technology, you will own the strategy and performance of our sales technology stack, building a connected, intelligent system that makes our sellers more effective at every stage of the sales cycle.

This is a technology leadership role with a clear mandate: define how our sellers work, wire that vision into the tools they use every day, and measure success by what happens in the field. You will report directly to the Senior Vice President of National Sales and be a key member of the national growth team. This role will partner closely with the National and Field Sales Leadership, Sales Operations, Head of Marketing Technology, Growth Marketing, and Learning & Development to ensure technology strategy translates into seller execution.

What You'll Own

Sales Technology Vision & Stack Strategy

In partnership with the national growth team, this role will own the end-to-end roadmap for our sales technology stack — how it's structured, how it evolves, the role of Ai and how it serves seller productivity at scale
Ensure our tools — ZoomInfo, MiEdge, Outreach, Seismic, and intent data platforms — operate as a connected system, not a collection of individual applications
Lead the strategic evaluation of AI-first versus technology-first solutions across the sales stack — defining a clear framework for when to buy, build, or integrate AI capabilities, what problems AI should solve versus traditional tooling, and how emerging AI solutions are assessed, piloted, and adopted in a way that creates measurable seller leverage
Define how data and signals flow across the stack, from buyer intent through rep action to pipeline outcome
Partner with the Head of Marketing Technology to align on shared data models, system integrations, and the handoff points where marketing infrastructure and sales technology meet — ensuring a seamless, connected GTM engine
Partner with IT, Legal and Compliance teams to ensure all sales technology adheres to organizational standards for data privacy, security, regulatory compliance, and brand integrity
Lead vendor relationships, renewals, and contract negotiations with a clear lens on ROI and strategic fit
Continuously evaluate the market for emerging tools and capabilities, particularly in AI, that create meaningful leverage for our sellers

Seller Effectiveness & Technology Adoption

Drive meaningful, measurable adoption of the sales technology stack across all seller segments — this means behavioral change, not just deployment
Partner with National and Field Sales Leadership to embed tools into daily seller workflows so technology becomes the way work gets done, not an add-on
Work alongside the Sales Enablement Coach to ensure the technology layer and producer coaching are aligned and mutually reinforcing
Partner with L&D to embed tool adoption into onboarding, Growth Academy cohorts, and ongoing producer development programs — so tools are taught in context, not in isolation
Serve as the connective layer between technology strategy and field execution — surfacing adoption gaps, workflow friction, and tool feedback back to internal teams continuously

AI-Enabled Selling

Drive the strategy for how AI creates leverage across the seller workflow, with a clear point of view on what to build, buy, adopt, or deprioritize
Own and evolve the AI sales tools already built in partnership with Product — serving as the business lead responsible for their ongoing development, adoption, and performance in the field
Operationalize intent data and AI-powered signals into actionable rep workflows and sequences through Outreach and ZoomInfo — integrating AI capabilities across the existing stack in ways that materially improve seller performance
Partner with Sales Leadership and the Sales Enablement Coach to ensure AI tools are embedded into seller workflows and coaching frameworks in a way that drives consistent, measurable behavior change
Align AI strategy with the Head of Marketing Technology to ensure a coordinated, enterprise-wide approach — avoiding parallel efforts and maximizing shared learnings across the GTM engine
Build internal fluency and confidence around AI tools — turning skepticism into daily habit across the sales team

Marketing & Signal Integration

Partner with Growth Marketing and the Head of Marketing Technology to connect marketing signals — intent data, campaigns, digital engagement — directly into seller workflows
Ensure producers are equipped to convert marketing-generated insights into pipeline opportunities through the right tools and sequences
Partner with Sales Operations to ensure the sales technology stack integrates seamlessly with our CRM ecosystem — owning the data flows, signal activation, and tool connections that turn CRM and third-party data into clear, actionable next steps for sellers
Collaborate with Sales Operations to ensure data integrity, pipeline visibility, and reporting frameworks support both field execution and leadership decision-making

Performance & ROI

Define and track utilization and performance metrics for every tool in the stack
Build reporting that connects technology adoption to pipeline and revenue outcomes
Own the technology budget with accountability for demonstrating return on every tool investment

Team Leadership

Leading by influence across complete sales and marketing organization
Build a culture of curiosity, experimentation, and seller empathy, a team that is always asking what's possible next

What We're Looking For

Experience

7+ years in sales technology, revenue operations, or sales enablement in a B2B environment
Deep hands-on experience with tools like Outreach, Seismic, ZoomInfo, and intent data platforms
Demonstrated experience applying AI tools to sales workflows — whether through AI-native platforms, embedded AI features, or custom implementations
Proven track record of driving technology adoption with skeptical sales teams — not just deploying software
Experience working cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, and Operations leadership at scale

Skills & Approach

You think in systems: you see how data, signals, and AI outputs flow from first touch to closed won
You speak both "sales" and "tech" fluently — sellers trust you, technical teams respect you, and leadership sees you as a strategic partner
You have a strong, informed point of view on where AI is creating real leverage in sales today — and where it's still hype
You are a builder — energized by creating structure, roadmaps, and capability where there isn't any
Strong analytical instincts — you connect technology investment to revenue outcomes and aren't satisfied with vanity metrics

Mindset

You believe the future of selling is tech-forward and AI-enabled — and you know how to bring people along on that journey
You treat adoption as a change management challenge, not a training problem
You are genuinely curious about what's next — you experiment, learn fast, and share what works
You are a collaborative partner to Sales leadership: opinionated, data-driven, and focused on their success

The typical base pay range for this role nationwide is $120,000 to $150,000 per year.

Your base pay is dependent upon your skills, education, qualifications, professional experience, and location. In addition to base pay, some roles are eligible for variable compensation, commission, and/or annual bonus based on your individual performance and/or the company’s performance. We also offer eligible employees health, wellbeing, retirement, and other financial benefits, paid time off, overtime pay for non-exempt employees, and robust learning and development programs. You will receive reimbursement of job-related expenses per the company policy and may receive employee perks and discounts.

To learn more, visit: www.onedigital.com/careers

jobs.title: Director of Professional Services
jobs.description:
Somewhere in your career, you walked into something that was already going wrong. A rollout three weeks from a date it was not going to hit. A team that had stopped telling anyone the truth about status. A client who had already decided you were the problem.

You did not wait for a playbook, because there was not one. You figured out what was actually broken, told people the parts they did not want to hear, and rebuilt the plan so it would hold this time. And when it landed, it landed because of how you ran it.

That is the kind of Director of Professional Services we are looking for.

What We Do

Every school district in America runs on service. Parents need answers, teachers need support, IT teams need systems that work. Most districts cobble that together with disconnected tools, overwhelmed staff, and no real visibility into what is working.

Onflo built the platform that fixes that. Our unified service platform brings together customer service, help desk ticketing, call center operations, AI chat, and IT asset management, purpose-built for K-12 public education. When a district runs on Onflo, their staff spends less time firefighting and more time serving students.

Professional Services is the team that makes that real. A district signs with us because they were promised something. Implementation, ongoing client solutioning, and client care all sit in this function, and together they decide whether that promise holds.

The Role

You would lead the function end to end. Roughly ten people across two layers, with four direct reports: three Implementation Managers, and the Manager of Professional Services who leads the Client Solutions Managers and Client Care Engineers.

The first year is largely about making the function current. Processes exist, but some were built for a smaller book of work and need modernizing. Newer systems do not have documented processes yet. Capacity is managed by judgment rather than a model. You would update what is there and build what is not, while the current book of delivery work keeps moving and districts keep going live. For the right person that is the appeal, not the catch.

What You Would Own

Delivery quality across implementation and ongoing solutioning engagements
Client care outcomes against service levels, delivered through the Manager of Professional Services
Post-implementation adoption, so districts realize the value they bought
Resource and capacity planning across the function
The methodology, templates, and standards the team runs on
Commercial performance of the function, including scoping, pricing, and margin, with the VP and Finance
Senior escalation point above the Implementation Manager and Manager level
Coaching and developing your direct reports

Who Thrives Here

We will be direct with you, because we think you will appreciate it.

Onflo is a small, entrepreneurial team in the middle of a rebrand and a change to how we deliver services. We do not have a perfect playbook. Priorities shift. Communication is not always tidy. Sales will sometimes scope something your team then has to deliver. Product will not always ship on the timeline you would hope. We know that, and we are actively working on it. What we do have is a product that genuinely helps schools, districts who trust us, and a team that cares about doing the work well.

The people who do their best work here build the thing that is missing rather than waiting for it. They are close to the work without taking it over, and they know the difference. They say the unpopular thing early, to Sales, to a district, to their own VP, and they say it without making it personal. They absorb pressure rather than passing it down, because escalations are a permanent feature of this function and the team takes its temperature from whoever is leading it. They take feedback and apply it, and they still hold a point of view.

If you have spent your career waiting for clear direction, a defined process, and stable priorities before you produce, this probably is not your role. If you have spent it figuring it out and delivering anyway, keep reading.

Two Ways In

We are running two candidate paths against the same bar, because the strongest delivery leaders come from two very different places. One is software: you have led implementation, professional services, or customer success inside a technology company. The other is the district side: you have led district-wide or multi-site operational, technical, or change initiatives from inside K-12, in IT, operations, or central-office leadership.

If you are coming from a district, your resume will not say "professional services" anywhere, and that is expected. We wrote our requirements around capabilities rather than job titles, and our screeners are instructed not to filter on vendor vocabulary. If you have run something district-wide from kickoff to the day it actually worked, apply.

What We Are Looking For

7 to 12 years of professional experience, including 5 to 8 years managing people directly
Personal ownership of a large-scale, multi-department rollout from kickoff through steady state, vendor-side or district-side
Experience building a process, playbook, or operational framework where none existed, and recovering something that was genuinely at risk of failing
A repeatable approach to making a new system stick past go-live, with a metric you moved
Ownership of operating metrics for a team you managed, including acting when one went the wrong way
Enough working knowledge of K-12 systems, single sign-on, student information systems, and data provisioning, to hold a credible conversation and know when to bring in a technical resource. Configuration depth is not required
Strong communication and stakeholder management, including with Sales and Finance
K-12 or EdTech experience on the vendor side is a plus, not a requirement
Able to travel 10% to 25% for internal meetings, conferences, industry events, and occasional on-site work with districts
The right person reading this already knows if they are right for it. If that is you, apply.

Compensation and Logistics

$135,000 to $160,000 base depending on experience, plus a discretionary annual bonus. Fully remote within the United States, with core operating hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern. A background check is required at offer, because districts set their own access requirements and we have to meet them.

Explore our website and LinkedIn to learn more about our work and impact.

jobs.title: Vice President, Technology, Innovation & AI
jobs.description:
Senior Associate, Corporate Partnerships

OVERALL POSITION DESCRIPTION

World Food Program USA mobilizes American policymakers, businesses and individuals to support the World Food Programme (WFP) in its mission to end hunger. The Vice President, Technology, Innovation and AI will help transform how the organization works, turning technology and innovation into greater capacity, stronger decisions and measurable mission impact.
Reporting to the Chief Operations Officer and Chief Financial Officer, the Vice President leads the IT, CRM and Data Analytics teams and advances the strategic plan by equipping staff with the tools, skills and trusted data to work more effectively. This leader sets and implements an enterprise technology vision, scales integrated data capabilities and embeds useful, responsible AI into everyday work. Success will be demonstrated through sustained staff adoption, measurable return on investment and reliable data integration that improves decisions and donor engagement.
The Vice President combines strategic leadership, business judgment and technical depth. They stay close enough to the work to evaluate architecture, challenge assumptions and guide consequential decisions, stepping in directly when needed. They deliver primarily through team leaders, staff and vendors, translating business needs into effective solutions and presenting progress, opportunities and risks to executive leadership and the Board as appropriate.

Why Join Us?

We are a dynamic, forward leaning, financially stable organization.
You will be joining an effective, committed, high-performing group of colleagues who are well-regarded in the community.
Your opinion will count, having exposure to key stakeholders in the company
You will have access to a host of inclusive benefits including parental leave, an EAP, and a wellness benefit.
You will play a crucial role in aiding the organization in their mission of ending global hunger.

About World Food Program USA

World Food Program USA’s values provide the framework for how we behave and work together to reach our goals to feed and save the lives of the most vulnerable people around the world. Those values are:
Collaborative
: We are all one team
Accountable
: We own our work
Respectful
: We are kind to each other
Inclusive
: We champion diversity
Optimistic
: We have a make it happen attitude

We are looking for applicants who embody these values and are invested in forwarding our mission.

Highlighted Responsibilities:

Turn strategy into measurable value

Develop and execute an enterprise technology, data and AI roadmap aligned with the strategic plan. Partner with department leaders to prioritize investments, sequence delivery and establish shared accountability for outcomes.
Build business cases with clear baselines, full implementation and operating costs, expected benefits and adoption measures. Track realized ROI with Finance and business owners, distinguishing financial savings from capacity gains and service improvements.
Set enterprise technology investment priorities and oversee the technology budget and vendor portfolio within delegated authority. Empower team leaders to manage delivery and assigned budgets. Partner with departments that hold technology budgets and ensure all technology selection, purchasing and implementation follows organizational processes, standards and protocols.

Make AI work for people

Lead substantial AI initiatives from opportunity assessment through deployment and sustained use across functions. Select practical use cases, test value and reliability, and scale solutions that demonstrate measurable benefits.
Partner with department leaders and People and Culture to build AI literacy and staff confidence through training, coaching, peer champions and hands-on demonstrations. Address barriers and use staff feedback to improve adoption.
Embed change management in every major initiative, including stakeholder engagement, workflow redesign, communications, training and post-launch support. Measure effective use and business outcomes beyond licenses issued or training completed.
Create a culture of thoughtful experimentation and continuous learning. Apply sound build-versus-buy judgment and guide teams and vendors toward maintainable solutions that fit organizational capacity.

Connect data to decisions

Lead the continued development and integration of enterprise platforms through the CRM and Data Analytics leaders, who own their respective platform roadmaps and delivery. Align their work to provide a secure, trusted view of donors and organizational performance.
Enable the Data Analytics team to scale reliable warehouse capabilities, data pipelines and integrations. Establish shared expectations for data quality, documentation and governance, with business stakeholders accountable for definitions and validation.
Partner with Development, Marketing and Communications, Public Policy, Finance and other teams to translate operational needs into useful analytics, dashboards, automation and AI-enabled workflows.
Set enterprise architecture principles and guide major platform and integration decisions. Establish one accountable technical owner for each integration across delivery, monitoring and ongoing support; resolve ownership and priority conflicts among IT, CRM and Data Analytics.

Build trust in technology

Lead and empower functional leaders to deliver reliable technology services and platforms. Set service expectations, cybersecurity and continuity priorities, and escalation thresholds; review performance across IT, CRM and Data Analytics and remove barriers to delivery.
Lead enterprise technology risk management, with IT responsible for shared infrastructure, identity and access, cybersecurity controls and incident readiness, and CRM and Data Analytics responsible for controls within their platforms. Escalate material risks and investment needs to the COO/CFO and relevant organizational leaders.
Establish and maintain best practices for technology, data and AI governance, including policy development, clear standards and decision authority, and monitoring of adherence and effectiveness. Partner with department leaders and relevant advisers to keep governance practical and responsive to evolving needs.

Grow talent and lead together

Attract, hire, develop and retain strong technical talent. Lead the leaders of IT, CRM and Data Analytics, organizing work around shared priorities and complementary strengths. Coach managers, support succession and hold teams accountable for delivery and service quality.
Build on the strengths of current teams, support professional growth and recommend how capabilities, capacity and ways of working can best advance the strategy.
Build trust across departments by listening to business needs, explaining tradeoffs clearly and resolving competing priorities with the COO/CFO and other leaders. Establish proactive staff communication about technology changes and disruptions, including why changes are happening, expected impact, timing, preparation and support. Ensure timely status updates and expected resolution or next-update times during disruptions.

A well-qualified candidate will possess the following:

Education

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience required.
Master’s degree in information systems, technology management, computer science, business administration or a related field preferred.

Years of experience

At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience, including at least eight years of people management experience.

Specific qualifications

Enterprise technology leadership spanning strategy, budgets, vendors, operations and the development of technical teams and managers.
Proven leadership of at least one substantial AI implementation that moved into regular business use, achieved widespread and sustained adoption, and produced measurable organizational results. Experience must extend beyond pilots and individual tool use.
Proven change-management leadership across departments, including stakeholder engagement, staff enablement, workflow change and measurement of sustained adoption.
Experience leading enterprise data warehouse implementation or modernization, integration and governance to provide reliable, accessible business information.
Deep technical judgment applied close to the work: evaluate architecture and integration choices, challenge vendor proposals and recognize when implementation needs intervention. Guide teams effectively and contribute directly when needed.
Sound business judgment: weigh mission impact, cost, risk, staff capacity and competing priorities; make timely decisions and assess whether investments deliver their intended value.
Ability to influence across departments, explain complex subjects clearly and build relationships with colleagues, executives and Board members.
Demonstrated ability to hire, develop and organize technical talent, including leading managers and building collaboration across disciplines. Lead with curiosity, accountability, inclusion and respect.
Experience leading the implementation and ongoing oversight of Microsoft Purview, including data classification, retention, data loss prevention, eDiscovery and related compliance controls.
Highly professional collaborator with personal integrity and discretion in handling confidential information; adaptable and comfortable with ambiguity; strong leadership presence and ability to influence others without direct authority.

Preferred qualifications

Substantial Salesforce experience, particularly CRM strategy, integration and adoption. Experience with Snowflake or a comparable enterprise data platform is also valuable.
Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization, with familiarity with fundraising, donor engagement or advocacy operations.
Relevant professional certification in change management, enterprise technology, data architecture or information security. Credentials complement demonstrated delivery and adoption experience.

Location and work arrangement

This position is based in the Washington, DC office and requires a minimum of three days per week in the office. Candidates must reside in the Washington, DC, Maryland or Virginia metropolitan area by their start date. Candidates willing to relocate are welcome; relocation assistance is not available.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Technology, Innovation & AI
new_jobs.description:
Senior Associate, Corporate Partnerships

OVERALL POSITION DESCRIPTION

World Food Program USA mobilizes American policymakers, businesses and individuals to support the World Food Programme (WFP) in its mission to end hunger. The Vice President, Technology, Innovation and AI will help transform how the organization works, turning technology and innovation into greater capacity, stronger decisions and measurable mission impact.
Reporting to the Chief Operations Officer and Chief Financial Officer, the Vice President leads the IT, CRM and Data Analytics teams and advances the strategic plan by equipping staff with the tools, skills and trusted data to work more effectively. This leader sets and implements an enterprise technology vision, scales integrated data capabilities and embeds useful, responsible AI into everyday work. Success will be demonstrated through sustained staff adoption, measurable return on investment and reliable data integration that improves decisions and donor engagement.
The Vice President combines strategic leadership, business judgment and technical depth. They stay close enough to the work to evaluate architecture, challenge assumptions and guide consequential decisions, stepping in directly when needed. They deliver primarily through team leaders, staff and vendors, translating business needs into effective solutions and presenting progress, opportunities and risks to executive leadership and the Board as appropriate.

Why Join Us?

We are a dynamic, forward leaning, financially stable organization.
You will be joining an effective, committed, high-performing group of colleagues who are well-regarded in the community.
Your opinion will count, having exposure to key stakeholders in the company
You will have access to a host of inclusive benefits including parental leave, an EAP, and a wellness benefit.
You will play a crucial role in aiding the organization in their mission of ending global hunger.

About World Food Program USA

World Food Program USA’s values provide the framework for how we behave and work together to reach our goals to feed and save the lives of the most vulnerable people around the world. Those values are:
Collaborative
: We are all one team
Accountable
: We own our work
Respectful
: We are kind to each other
Inclusive
: We champion diversity
Optimistic
: We have a make it happen attitude

We are looking for applicants who embody these values and are invested in forwarding our mission.

Highlighted Responsibilities:

Turn strategy into measurable value

Develop and execute an enterprise technology, data and AI roadmap aligned with the strategic plan. Partner with department leaders to prioritize investments, sequence delivery and establish shared accountability for outcomes.
Build business cases with clear baselines, full implementation and operating costs, expected benefits and adoption measures. Track realized ROI with Finance and business owners, distinguishing financial savings from capacity gains and service improvements.
Set enterprise technology investment priorities and oversee the technology budget and vendor portfolio within delegated authority. Empower team leaders to manage delivery and assigned budgets. Partner with departments that hold technology budgets and ensure all technology selection, purchasing and implementation follows organizational processes, standards and protocols.

Make AI work for people

Lead substantial AI initiatives from opportunity assessment through deployment and sustained use across functions. Select practical use cases, test value and reliability, and scale solutions that demonstrate measurable benefits.
Partner with department leaders and People and Culture to build AI literacy and staff confidence through training, coaching, peer champions and hands-on demonstrations. Address barriers and use staff feedback to improve adoption.
Embed change management in every major initiative, including stakeholder engagement, workflow redesign, communications, training and post-launch support. Measure effective use and business outcomes beyond licenses issued or training completed.
Create a culture of thoughtful experimentation and continuous learning. Apply sound build-versus-buy judgment and guide teams and vendors toward maintainable solutions that fit organizational capacity.

Connect data to decisions

Lead the continued development and integration of enterprise platforms through the CRM and Data Analytics leaders, who own their respective platform roadmaps and delivery. Align their work to provide a secure, trusted view of donors and organizational performance.
Enable the Data Analytics team to scale reliable warehouse capabilities, data pipelines and integrations. Establish shared expectations for data quality, documentation and governance, with business stakeholders accountable for definitions and validation.
Partner with Development, Marketing and Communications, Public Policy, Finance and other teams to translate operational needs into useful analytics, dashboards, automation and AI-enabled workflows.
Set enterprise architecture principles and guide major platform and integration decisions. Establish one accountable technical owner for each integration across delivery, monitoring and ongoing support; resolve ownership and priority conflicts among IT, CRM and Data Analytics.

Build trust in technology

Lead and empower functional leaders to deliver reliable technology services and platforms. Set service expectations, cybersecurity and continuity priorities, and escalation thresholds; review performance across IT, CRM and Data Analytics and remove barriers to delivery.
Lead enterprise technology risk management, with IT responsible for shared infrastructure, identity and access, cybersecurity controls and incident readiness, and CRM and Data Analytics responsible for controls within their platforms. Escalate material risks and investment needs to the COO/CFO and relevant organizational leaders.
Establish and maintain best practices for technology, data and AI governance, including policy development, clear standards and decision authority, and monitoring of adherence and effectiveness. Partner with department leaders and relevant advisers to keep governance practical and responsive to evolving needs.

Grow talent and lead together

Attract, hire, develop and retain strong technical talent. Lead the leaders of IT, CRM and Data Analytics, organizing work around shared priorities and complementary strengths. Coach managers, support succession and hold teams accountable for delivery and service quality.
Build on the strengths of current teams, support professional growth and recommend how capabilities, capacity and ways of working can best advance the strategy.
Build trust across departments by listening to business needs, explaining tradeoffs clearly and resolving competing priorities with the COO/CFO and other leaders. Establish proactive staff communication about technology changes and disruptions, including why changes are happening, expected impact, timing, preparation and support. Ensure timely status updates and expected resolution or next-update times during disruptions.

A well-qualified candidate will possess the following:

Education

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience required.
Master’s degree in information systems, technology management, computer science, business administration or a related field preferred.

Years of experience

At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience, including at least eight years of people management experience.

Specific qualifications

Enterprise technology leadership spanning strategy, budgets, vendors, operations and the development of technical teams and managers.
Proven leadership of at least one substantial AI implementation that moved into regular business use, achieved widespread and sustained adoption, and produced measurable organizational results. Experience must extend beyond pilots and individual tool use.
Proven change-management leadership across departments, including stakeholder engagement, staff enablement, workflow change and measurement of sustained adoption.
Experience leading enterprise data warehouse implementation or modernization, integration and governance to provide reliable, accessible business information.
Deep technical judgment applied close to the work: evaluate architecture and integration choices, challenge vendor proposals and recognize when implementation needs intervention. Guide teams effectively and contribute directly when needed.
Sound business judgment: weigh mission impact, cost, risk, staff capacity and competing priorities; make timely decisions and assess whether investments deliver their intended value.
Ability to influence across departments, explain complex subjects clearly and build relationships with colleagues, executives and Board members.
Demonstrated ability to hire, develop and organize technical talent, including leading managers and building collaboration across disciplines. Lead with curiosity, accountability, inclusion and respect.
Experience leading the implementation and ongoing oversight of Microsoft Purview, including data classification, retention, data loss prevention, eDiscovery and related compliance controls.
Highly professional collaborator with personal integrity and discretion in handling confidential information; adaptable and comfortable with ambiguity; strong leadership presence and ability to influence others without direct authority.

Preferred qualifications

Substantial Salesforce experience, particularly CRM strategy, integration and adoption. Experience with Snowflake or a comparable enterprise data platform is also valuable.
Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization, with familiarity with fundraising, donor engagement or advocacy operations.
Relevant professional certification in change management, enterprise technology, data architecture or information security. Credentials complement demonstrated delivery and adoption experience.

Location and work arrangement

This position is based in the Washington, DC office and requires a minimum of three days per week in the office. Candidates must reside in the Washington, DC, Maryland or Virginia metropolitan area by their start date. Candidates willing to relocate are welcome; relocation assistance is not available.

HOW TO APPLY

Please submit a resume and cover letter to the link provided. No phone calls or agencies, please.
